results.title: Pan-cancer proteogenomics connects oncogenic drivers to ...
results.content: # Article Pan-cancer proteogenomics connects oncogenic drivers to functional states. Here, our multi-omics pan-cancer analysis uncovers insights into the impacts of cancer drivers by identifying their significant *cis*-effects and distal *trans*-effects quantified at the RNA, protein, and phosphoprotein levels. Raw and processed proteomics as well as open-access genomic data, can be obtained via Proteomic Data Commons (PDC) at . Complete CPTAC pan-cancer controlled and processed data can be accessed via the Cancer Data Service (CDS: ). The CPTAC pan-cancer data hosted in CDS is controlled data and can be accessed through the NCI DAC approved, dbGaP compiled whitelists. Users can access the data for analysis through the Seven Bridges Cancer Genomics Cloud (SB-CGC) which is one of the NCI-funded Cloud Resource/platform for compute intensive analysis. Log into CGC to access Cancer Data Service (CDS) File Explore 4. We focused on the CPTAC samples with both genomic and proteomic data available to investigate the pan-cancer proteogenomic impacts of oncogenic drivers.
